summary: Despite sharing its name with one of the world's most famous music festivals — held just northwest of city limits at the Empire Polo Club — Coachella the city is fundamentally an agricultural town planted on the flat, sun-scorched floor of the eastern Coachella Valley, where date palm groves and irrigated farmland stretch toward the Chocolate Mountains to the east and the Santa Rosa range to the west. The economy leans heavily on agriculture and its supporting logistics and service sectors, meaning job-switching without a commute often requires heading 20-plus miles northwest toward Palm Desert or Indio along Interstate 10, the valley's single arterial spine. With a median home price around $341,300 against a median household income of roughly $67,600, the price-to-income ratio sits near 5:1 — tight but far more approachable than coastal California, and monthly rents averaging $1,115 leave noticeably more breathing room. Daily life unfolds under relentless sunshine — an annual average high of 84°F masks summer stretches well above 110°F, which compresses outdoor activity into mornings and late evenings for several months. The street grid is largely low-slung and car-dependent, with limited pedestrian infrastructure connecting subdivisions to commercial strips. Coachella is a place defined by the tension between rapid residential growth and the agricultural economy that still shapes its rhythms and landscape.
